title: flow-review-config/0
description: flow-review.config.json: what a flow without its own app runs against, per surface. The nearest one above a flow file applies.

ready.description: A URL that answers once the app is up (default: url), or "stdout-json": up when it prints a JSON object line, whose fields become ${start.<field>}.

target.description: The default target when neither --target nor FLOW_REVIEW_TARGET is given.

cli.description: agent-cli: the command each run step's argv follows, such as ["node", "${target}"].

cliNames.description: Command names a stderr line may name as the fix (the namesFix rule).

controlUrl.description: A mock's control port, for harness steps.

stateProbe.description: agent-cli: argv (after app.cli) whose output must not change across a readOnly flow.

guard.description: argv run once the app is up; it must exit 0 (for example, a check that it is a mock).

files.description: Files written (relative to the working directory) before the app starts.

help.description: agent-cli: argv (after cli) that prints the top-level help; every command a flow runs successfully must be listed in it (the listed check).

scope.description: run (default): one app for every flow that starts it the same way; flow: a fresh one for each flow.

vars.description: Values for {name} placeholders in steps (saves add to them).

cellMs.description: The most one matrix cell (or agent unit) may take, its app start included (default 120000). Past it the cell is stopped (its page closed, its commands killed), a timeout finding names the step it was on, and the run goes on with the next cell.

stepMs.description: The most one step may take (default 60000): a hung goto, act or waitFor fails that step, naming its target. A waitFor with a longer ms gets that ms and 5 s more; an agent step's own timeoutMs wins.

timeouts.description: Time limits for this config's web flows, over the config's own.

failOn.description: What fails the run for this config's web flows, over the config's own: any, none or a comma list of checks, in place of --fail-on. A flow that fails on nothing is advisory: when merge finds its cells missing, run twice or timed out, they become coverage findings, not a failed merge.
